facts.claim: Zhang et al. (ICML 2025) gathered 184 failed tasks from 127 multi-agent systems, each labelled with the agent and the step that caused the failure.
Zhang et al. (ICML 2025): the best automatic method named the agent at fault 53.5% of the time, but the step that caused the failure only 14.2%.
Zhang et al. (ICML 2025) call a mistake decisive if fixing it turns the failed run into a success; when several are, the earliest is the cause.
Labelling those failures by hand took the paper’s three people about 84 hours between them, and each was unsure on 15–30% of cases (Zhang et al., ICML 2025).
Zhang et al. (ICML 2025): even strong reasoning models, OpenAI o1 and DeepSeek R1 among them, were not yet good enough at finding the failing step to use in practice.
Principles of Chaos Engineering (last updated March 2019): experiment on a system to build confidence it can withstand rough conditions in production.
Principles of Chaos Engineering: bring in real-world events, such as servers that crash, then look for a difference from the system’s normal behaviour.
Netflix’s Chaos Monkey switches off machines in production at random, so engineers meet failures often and build services that survive them.
Yao et al. (τ-bench, 2024): gpt-4o succeeded on under half the tasks, and on retail tasks got all 8 tries of the same task right under 25% of the time.
